candidates.title: Review article on energy conversion in fusion power plants (Rankine/Brayton cycles, structural material temperature limits)
candidates.notes: Open-access review article discussing thermal efficiency limits from irradiated structural materials in water-cooled fusion reactors; abstract confirms discussion of WCLL-relevant temperature constraints and overall thermal efficiency. Directly relevant to sourcing the ~32% efficiency inference for Stellaris EUROFER97+WCLL.

candidates.title: Comparison of leading candidate combinations of blanket materials, thermodynamic cycles, and tritium systems for full scale fusion power plants
candidates.notes: OSTI conference paper on blanket+cycle combinations — potentially directly addresses WCLL thermal efficiency. Not triaged in depth; saved as candidate for future iteration if arxiv-1401-4232 insufficient.

candidates.title: Thermo-structural design of the European DEMO water-cooled blanket (OSTI)
candidates.notes: WCLL thermo-structural design paper — likely contains coolant outlet temperatures and thermal cycle assumptions. Paywalled journal article; OSTI page may have abstract only.

gaps_attempted.notes: Extracted an open-access review paper on fusion power plant thermal cycles that discusses efficiency limits from structural material temperature constraints. This provides a citable basis for the ~30-35% efficiency inference for WCLL+EUROFER97 configurations. Stellaris-specific thermal efficiency not publicly disclosed; Helios analogue (40%) remains the best proxy for WCLL-alternative designs. G-4 remains not-fully-closed but now has a sourced engineering basis for the 32% estimate.

candidates.title: World Nuclear News: German stellarator fusion design concept unveiled
candidates.notes: Article fetched — only high-level qualitative description of Stellaris. No Q value or ECRH data. Mentions Alpha demo for Q>1 in 2031.

candidates.title: IEEE Spectrum: Stellarator Showdown — Proxima vs. Type One Energy
candidates.notes: JS-heavy page — article body not extractable; only schema metadata and JavaScript framework present.

gaps_attempted.notes: Q value and post-ignition ECRH requirement are not disclosed in any accessible public source. The Stellaris paper (FED Vol. 214, DOI: 10.1016/j.fusengdes.2025.114868) is paywalled; the KIT repository version already extracted as stellaris-design-details.md is the most complete open-access version. The paper states 50 MW ECRH operational power but does not publish Q; Alpha demo (2031) targets Q>1 confirmation. No open-access preprint of the Stellaris paper found on arxiv. G-6 remains open and inaccessible without institutional access to FED.

W7-X Wendelstein 7-X "50 non-planar coils" OR "50 modular coils" coil mass kg manufacturing cost stellarator

candidates.title: Wikipedia: Wendelstein 7-X
candidates.notes: W7-X is the direct experimental predecessor to Stellaris (Proxima Fusion is a W7-X/IPP spin-off). Contains coil count (50 non-planar + 20 planar = 70 total), cold mass (~425 metric tons for full magnet system), and engineering construction details. Useful as quantitative proxy for G-11 coil count and per-coil mass analogue.

candidates.title: Fabrication of the superconducting coils for Wendelstein 7-X (ScienceDirect)
candidates.notes: Primary W7-X coil fabrication paper — paywalled on ScienceDirect. ResearchGate mirror returned 403.

candidates.title: Fusion Energy Insights: Analysis of Proxima Fusion Stellaris
candidates.notes: Fetched — no specific technical parameters; directs to in-depth analysis not included on page.

gaps_attempted.notes: W7-X Wikipedia provides a useful proxy for G-11: 50 non-planar + 20 planar superconducting coils, ~425 metric ton total cold mass (~6-8.5 tons per non-planar coil as rough proxy). Stellaris-specific coil count and per-coil mass are not in any public source found; Stellaris §2.11 (remote maintenance) is the authoritative reference but remains paywalled. The W7-X analogue is LTS, not HTS, and at different scale — treat as structural proxy only. G-11 remains partial.
